title: XMRIG Web API not starting when using wireless connection
body:
I am running xmrig on a machine that uses a wireless connection, debian 10, when the machine boots, it takes it a short time to connect to the wifi hotspot. XMRIG is set to auto start using the @reboot in crontab, and specifying cli options to connect to the xmrig-proxy.

The problem arises, when it reboots/starts up, it runs xmrig, and all is good, with the exception of the web api interface, the web server does not start up. (xmrig is mining, just no web api) I tried starting xmrig manually using the same exact command in crontab, and it works great, starting xmrig along with the web api

Added  sleep 60 && before the crontab command, and poof, it works fine.

It appears that if there is no network connection, the web api wont start up, even if the web connection appears after a short connection time. Is there a solution that can be put into xmrig to have it try again to start the api, or put in a cli option to wait a short time to start to give the network time to come alive?

the wireless connection is set up using a static ip for the machine, so it knows what IP address it should have when it starts up.

comments.body:
Stop (ab)using cron and make a real systemd service.

Put this in `/lib/systemd/system/xmrig.service`:
```
[Unit]
Description=xmrig
After=network-online.target systemd-modules-load.service
Wants=network-online.target systemd-modules-load.service
AssertFileNotEmpty=/opt/xmrig/config.json

[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
Group=root
Restart=always
KillSignal=SIGINT
LimitMEMLOCK=8G
WorkingDirectory=/opt/xmrig
SyslogIdentifier=xmrig
TimeoutStartSec=30s
TimeoutStopSec=15s
ExecStart=/opt/xmrig/xmrig

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Then `systemctl daemon-reload` and then `systemctl restart xmrig` and then `journalctl -n50 -xafu xmrig` will show what's happening.

The first couple lines tell it not to launch before network-online status.
Oh and obviously if your install folder is not `/opt/xmrig` then mass replace with wherever.

i wouldn't call it abusing cron, making it run as a service would be a royal pita to set up (im running 170+ machines), crontab is the simple solution to launching it.

title: Is there any reason 'qbt torrent list' wouldn't work with cron?
body:
I'm having trouble getting this to run with cron on Debian Buster on my Raspberry Pi. Running `/usr/bin/qbt torrent list` works fine as user/sudo, and I'm able to redirect the output to a log with no problem. But when I add it to `crontab -e`:

`* * * * *    /usr/bin/qbt torrent list >> /home/pi/LOG.log 2>&1`

The log file is created, but the output of the command does not log. I've tried copying the cron environment and running the command manually. With `crontab -e`, I added:

`* * * * * env > ~/cronenv`

Then run:
``env - `cat ~/cronenv` /bin/sh``
`/usr/bin/qbt torrent list`

It runs fine and outputs as expected, but when I try to redirect the output to a log, log is created but empty:
`/usr/bin/qbt torrent list >> LOG.log`

If I prepend with an `unbuffer` in this environment, the log is populated appropriately:
`/usr/bin/unbuffer /usr/bin/qbt torrent list >> LOG.log`

But even with the unbuffer, it's still not working in crontab. I've also tried  `bash -l -c -x '/usr/bin/qbt torrent list'`, changing the cron shell (SHELL=/bin/bash), adding my path to cron, etc. but nothing works. I even have a Python script that calls qbt; the Python script works fine when I run it normally, the script runs fine in cron (and logging the output works fine), but the call from the script always returns `output=b""` and `error=None`:

    `process = subprocess.Popen("/usr/bin/unbuffer /usr/bin/qbt torrent list", stdout=subprocess.PIPE, shell=True)`
    `output, error = process.communicate()`

When I try to run this command through a single SSH command, it works (e.g. `ssh pi@pi2.lan` -t '/usr/bin/qbt torrent list'`), but not when I attempt to launch the SSH command through that system's cron (though other SSH commands through cron work fine). 

What am I missing?

comments.body:
I've run into the same issue on Debian 11 (bullseye). I'm currently running the commands through PowerShell (pwsh) and they work when called manually, but always get an empty result in cron.

@TheFrostyboss did you ever find a solution?
You can try to run [it](https://github.com/fedarovich/qbittorrent-cli/wiki/qbt-torrent-list) with output in JSON (`--format json`) or CSV (`--format csv`) format. I think it should work in this case.

I was using `--format json` for part of my script, and it looks like that part is working. I initially had some code to grab the pretty print table and include it in a file, but after flipping it to just use the json object everything appears to be working.

Here is a snippet of my powershell that I ended up using to get a formatted table:
```powershell
$stalledTorrents = qbt torrent list --filter stalledDownloading --format json | ConvertFrom-Json
$stalledTorrentsTable = $stalledTorrents | Sort-Object -Property added_on | Format-Table state,name,@{Label="progress"; Expression={$_.progress.tostring("P2")}}
$stalledTorrentsTable | Out-File ...
```

Thanks for the tip.

Hi,

Have you some more logs to provide? For instance logs from `php-errors.log`.

A common mistake it to execute the cron using another user than the one associated to the webserver (`www-data` per default). Could you ensure that the crontab is associated to this user, and that all GLPI files are owned by this user?

accidentally closed it before commending. I will write down my steps and close the thread again.

@ebouda33 Thanks allot for the help!

My steps are as follows: 

I created the **pcloud.sh** file. You can have it wherever you like, mine is in **/home/user/startupCommands/**

pcloud.sh
`
#! /bin/sh

the -m /home/user/pcloud is where I wanted to mount my pcloud drive.


Then I created the service file (pcloud.service) in the /etc/systemd/system/

pcloud.service

Group=[MY_USER]

`

After that I executed the following commands

if you don't want to reboot your system then execute the following command as well
`sudo systemctl start pcloud`

and that is it!

The pcloud script works like a charm when in the command line...
In Service, it is not working...no message of error.

When I restart the computer, the pCloudDrive does not appear in Nautilus.

pcloud.service
```
[Service]
User=parallels 
Group=parallels 
ExecStart=/home/parallels/startup/pcloud.sh
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

pcloud.sh
```
#! /bin/sh 
echo "password" | pcloudcc -u user@domain -p -d -m /home/parallels/pCloudDrive
```

nothing happens when I do:
```
parallels@ubuntu-linux-20-04-desktop:~$ sudo systemctl enable pcloud
parallels@ubuntu-linux-20-04-desktop:~$ sudo systemctl start pcloud
```
but happens when:
`./startup/pcloud.sh
`

This is the output of `sudo systemctl status pcloud`
```
● pcloud.service
     Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/pcloud.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
     Active: inactive (dead) since Tue 2023-01-31 14:07:52 -03; 1min 53s ago

I found the solution...

The pcloud.service must be:
```
[Service]
User=parallels
Group=parallels
Type=simple
RemainAfterExit=yes
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Just add `RemainAfterExit=yes` and `Type=simple`

title: Can't control swww using cron
body:
Hello I want to switch my wallpapers for example every hour using cron, but it seems I can't control swww using it.

What I do:
``exec=swww init`` in my wayland compositor's config

And the script that I launch in crontab:
```
/home/SDD/.local/bin/wal -i /home/SDD/Wallpapers/
swww img "$(< "/home/SDD/.cache/wal/wal")"
```

Logs of the script execution:
```
Error: "Socket file not found. Are you sure swww-daemon is running?"
```

If I kill/init swww in the script I get the same error, but when I launch it from terminal all works fine. Am I missing something or this is a bug? Thank you in advance.

comments.body: If the script is telling you the daemon isn't running, then the problem is that `exec=swww init` isn't working. This can sometimes happen if the compositor runs these commands before the whole compositor state is set up (so `swww` can't listen in to output yet, for example). I think someone else had a similar problem before, I'll see if I can find it.
The only way to do that is to check if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set before running `swww`

This can sometimes happen if the compositor runs these commands before the whole compositor state is set up (so `swww` can't listen in to output yet, for example). I think someone else had a similar problem before, I'll see if I can find it.

I've forgotten to mention, swww img is working with this exec, I can use swww img interactively.  Also if I try to not init it in exec, but in the cron script, even for the first time the log outputs:

```
Error: "Failed to connect to socket: Connection refused (os error 111)"

```

> The only way to do that is to check if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set before running `swww`

My WAYLAND_DISPLAY is "wayland-1". I've added this in the compositor's config before swww init: 
```
exec=export WAYLAND_DISPLAY="wayland-1"
```
and in the script that cron is launching:
```
export WAYLAND_DISPLAY="wayland-1"
```
but it seems still not working. Am I doing it wrong?

After executing this in the script:
```
rm -vrf /tmp/swww && export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="/run/user/1000" && swww init --no-daemon
```

I see this output in the logs, despite I've completely removed any inits from compositor's config (the compositor is running):
```
removed '/tmp/swww/swww.socket'
removed directory '/tmp/swww'
thread 'main' panicked at 'Failed to connect to wayland environment: NoCompositorListening', daemon/src/wayland.rs:51:45
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

Maybe it could help

> > The only way to do that is to check if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set before running `swww`
> 
> My WAYLAND_DISPLAY is "wayland-1". I've added this in the compositor's config before swww init:
> 
> ```
> exec=export WAYLAND_DISPLAY="wayland-1"
> ```
> 
> and in the script that cron is launching:
> 
> ```
> export WAYLAND_DISPLAY="wayland-1"
> ```
> 
> but it seems still not working. Am I doing it wrong?

you're doing it wrong. What i meant was if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is *set by a compositor*, run `swww`

You shouldn't set the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` yourself as that is set by the Wayland compositor you are using. Unless you are spawning stuff from a running Wayland compositor while you are in a different tty session assuming you know what value their `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is. You can also use a systemd.timer as well and make it run only if `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is available.

So, I've done some research. The problem was the limited environment that crontab runs on. So cycle sleep until `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set is pointless, because cron job wouldn't see it anyway (despite whoami returns my login when running a cron script). Setting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` in crontab doesn't help too, because cron job still can't locate the running daemon. Possible workaround is to use `at` command to set up a schedule  in the script and then run it when the compositor is starting up. 

If this would work, I'll paste here my files, so anyone for the same problem could use it, If it would have the same problems, then I guess swww is not designed for that kind of automation and I need to PR/fork some fixes to locate existing daemon and control it in any environment

outside ~, they are not assigned a proper label (which means, not

why everything works fine if I use midnight commander ("mc") [1] in a

always worked with "mc".

I just tested with "mc" and evaluated the root logs: The very first time 
when I used "mc" to move a file (a file that makes dolphin crash) in 
this KDE session, it logged a comparable dbus-broker denial as dolphin,

file works fine as well. In all later tries to move files that make

everything worked fine. Interesting behavior.

some other limitations, too (e.g., staff_u cannot `> /dev/*` in a terminal).

I have been playing with potential mitigations for the two related 
issues: one one hand, the fact that SELinux seems to not create 
appropriate labels automatically for files/folders that are created by 
non-root user accounts outside their own home dir (even if they own the 
superordinated dirs). On the other hand, the issue that I still need to 
use permanently sysadm_u for productive working because of permanent 
work with folder/files outside my home.

I cannot just put the folders/files into my ~ for several reasons 
(ironically primarily security reasons). However, I was trying to mount 
the folders into my ~ with `mount --bind /outside-home-path/ 
~/within-home-path`. However, when creating new files, now seemingly 
within ~, SELinux did still assign the labels as if I had created the 
files outside ~. It remains impressive how hard it is to distract 
SELinux. Yet, do you maybe have another idea that could work to achieve 
that?

I assume it would also mitigate the issue of the ticket, and might 
present a solution for people who have to work outside their ~ 
directories while working in confined user accounts. Just in case it 
proves not realistic to make SELinux create appropriate labels 
automatically in the mentioned circumstances.

SELinux label everything be

I found the origin of the inappropriate automatic labeling and thus the unintended SELinux denials: the superordinated directory outside ~ that does belong to the user just like ~ needs to be `user_home_dir_t` (with "dir" in the middle; just like ~) instead of `user_home_t`. This will ensure that auto-labeling is done properly in subordinated paths so that everything works and remains aligned.

The issue that `dolphin` breaks in operations (which are still possible even with the improper auto-labeling when `user_home_dir_t` is not set -  as it is proven by, e.g., `mc`) seems to occur just because `dolphin` does not consider the output it gets in this situation and thus the `dolphin` issue is not related to this topic as long as `dolphin` is not intended to officially support confined user accounts.

Another advantage achieved that way is that I can now also downgrade my user privileges to staff_u and user_u.

However, there is nearly no documentation available of the dynamics/differences of `user_home_dir_t` and `user_home_t`, and nearly nothing about `user_home_dir_t` at all. I am not sure if that would be something to forward upstream?

However, this labeling solves the topic for me. I assume it does not need a general adjustment for Fedora because this use case/situation does not appear on default Fedora installations. body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When you deploy the collector, you have no feedback that it really works besides the lonely message `starting cron`.
You can play with the cron schedule to test it faster then change it back which is quite some useless work.
You can also access the container and run it manually `scrutiny-collector-metrics run` which is also useless extra work.

It would be better if the collector runs once immediately at deployment to provide an immediate feedback

Well, maybe run it after a certain delay 20-30s since in swarm mode, the `depends_on` is not supported so if it starts immediately it might be unable to reach the end point which is still starting up).

`ENV_VAR` can be used as well to enable the first run as well as fix the delay duration (in seconds).

**Additional context**
-/-

comments.body:
Great idea. Implemented via 2 env variables - `COLLECTOR_RUN_STARTUP` and `COLLECTOR_RUN_STARTUP_SLEEP`.

Please note, this only applies to the `collector` docker image.

@AnalogJ Why not default true? It's a bit confusing since the option is hardly documented (only mentioned in troubleshooting docs), plus in #95 this was enabled by default.

I propose either changing it to true by default, or at least adjusting default docker-compose example files to both include `COLLECTOR_RUN_STARTUP=false` in their environment section, so that users see this exists and can easily adjust it to true when setting it up.
@p0358 good callout. I just updated the example docker-compose file with the env variable and a link to the troubleshooting docs.

body:
I've hit a transient problem renewing a cert with Let's Encrypt.  The following log is from the `acme.sh --cron` session (mildly redacted):

Checking the same URL manually a few minutes later gave me a valid signed cert, so it looks as though the signing succeeded, but the request to actually download the issued cert yielded a 404.

Other renewals in the same cron session worked just fine, and I'm sure next time the cronjob runs, the failed renewal will work too - this seems to be a rare problem.  But the cert issued originally is now effectively wasted, as I guess the next run will start again with a fresh key and CSR.

Short of running _all_ renewals with debug on for weeks in the hope that the problem recurs, I don't think I can gather any more useful data than I already have, unfortunately. title: Problem when running goaccess with cron
body:
I have the following script `updateStats.sh` that works great when I run it manually but fails when run on Ubuntu via cron with `0 * * * * /var/www/html/updateStats.sh`

`cat updateStats.sh`:

```
goaccess /var/log/nginx/access.log -o /var/www/html/nginxDaily.html --log-format=COMBINED --anonymize-ip
zcat -f /var/log/nginx/access.log* | goaccess -o /var/www/html/nginxDailyAll.html --log-format=COMBINED --anonymize-ip
```

`cat cron.log` provides:

```
 [PARSING /var/log/nginx/access.log] {4907} @ {0/s}
Cleaning up resources...

GoAccess - version 1.5.5 - Feb  5 2022 18:37:15
Config file: /etc/goaccess/goaccess.conf

Fatal error has occurred
Error occurred at: src/goaccess.c - initializer - 1457
No input data was provided nor there's data to restore.
```

The first line runs fine. The second line fails.

Any ideas what I'm doing wrong?

comments.body:
Great question. When piping data to goaccess via the cron or pretty much anytime you pipe data in, you will need to add a dash. e.g., 

    zcat -f /var/log/nginx/access.log* | goaccess - -o /var/www/html/nginxDailyAll.html --log-format=COMBINED --anonymize-ip

Let me know if that helps.
@allinurl that seemed to work! Thanks so much!
Glad that worked :)

Hi - just run into it and was almost before opening an issue for it. Glad to found the solution among the closed ones. (Can confirm it, too). The behavior though seems strange, if the single ssh command works but not while executed during cron....hm for better understanding can someone explain what is happening here? 

Anyway THX for the solution :-)

@StefanSchubert cron doesn't give a TTY so [`isatty(3)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/isatty.3.html) fails when no filename is passed and thus it won't output a report. A single dash (`-`), with no option, [usually means "read from standard input"](https://unix.stackexchange.com/q/16357/22222). This is a very common convention used by many programs. Hope that helps clarify this.
@allinurl Did it! Thanks for the explanation - I learned something new by it!
great explanation. It solves my issues. :-)

### Describe the bug

When deploying the app with the default settings the root filesystem is read-only. The way webgrab+ needs to be operated requires running an update script through a cron-job. This script accesses files from the /app folder and crashes with an error because of the read-only filesystem. Also there will be no creation of the xml file or checking the license used to be valid. Basically the container cannot be used as intended unless the expert options are chosen not to write protect the root filesystem. Once it can be written everything works fine.

### To Reproduce

Deploy the container with the default (write protected root filesystem)
Enter the container and create a valid config file that can be used to grab the EPG information.
Manually run the update.sh script from the /default folder.

### Expected Behavior

The update script runs fine, checks the license and starts downloading the EPG information from the configured source.

### Screenshots

Not applicable

### Additional Context

Since the root filesystem is read only and the actual app seems to be located under the /app folder it cannot write anything. Obviously the mono framework once launched needs to write something into the /app folder and therefore it crashes as it cannot write in there.

- [X] I've checked all open and closed issues and my issue is not there.

title: No warning when cronjobs won’t run due to a configuration error
body:
# Edit:

I configured a scheduled backup for PostgreSQL and noticed it failed to run. Executing the backup job manually from the backup configuration page or from the cronjob page worked.

Investigation revealed that this was caused by a world-readable root crontab. Changing permissions fixed things—but it was difficult to figure out, and Webmin didn’t provide a clue at what was wrong.

Ask Ubuntu has a list of common cron gotchas at https://askubuntu.com/questions/23009/why-crontab-scripts-are-not-working (most of which presumably apply equally to other distros and even other Unices). Maybe Webmin could warn about the most common/easy-to-catch ones and offer to fix them. I had to dig down quite deep to find out what was wrong, and I assume the whole point of Webmin is to avoid having to do this :-)

# Original report:

Steps to reproduce:

* Set up PostgreSQL.
* Configure global backup in Webmin. Make sure the backup directory has correct permissions (see #855).
* Perform a manual backup, verify backup files get created, and delete the backup files again.
* Schedule a backup for the near future.

Expected behavior:

* Successful backup at the scheduled time

Actual behavior:

* Nothing happens. No files are created, the cron log is empty (I have enabled it before).

Additional information:

When I go to the backup cronjob in Webmin and run it manually, the backup succeeds.

The cronjob is owned by `root` but the resulting files are owned by `postgres`, indicating that a user context change takes place here (which is necessary as `root` usually has no permission within PostgreSQL).

cron itself seems to work correctly, as I get notifications about package updates (which, as far as I can see, are also handled via a cronjob).

System configuration:

    Server side: Raspbian Squeeze, Webmin 1.880, PostgreSQL 9.6.6
    Client side: Ubuntu MATE 16.04, Firefox 58.0.2 (64-bit)

Just came across something:

    cron[322]: (root) INSECURE MODE (mode 0600 expected) (crontabs/root)

Apparently the crontab had incorrect permissions set. To rectify:

    sudo chmod 600 /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root
    sudo touch /var/spool/cron/crontabs

Then I rescheduled the backup and verified that the crontab permissions were still correct. This time the backup was executed correctly.

So ultimately the issue was the crontab permissions. I am positive I did not change them manually, and the system is quite fresh (set up a week ago)—either the permissions were incorrect out of the box, or one of the packages I installed messed with them.

However, this is a common gotcha (for a more elaborate list, see https://askubuntu.com/questions/23009/why-crontab-scripts-are-not-working). Maybe Webmin could warn about the most common/easy-to-catch ones and offer to fix them. I had to dig down quite deep to find out what was wrong, and I assume the whole point of Webmin is to avoid having to do this :-)

I have detected that in js rules and in windows environments, the value of time.toZDT() is not updated after the operating system is synchronized with the time server (NTP). This causes the value to be ahead or behind (depending on the computer).

title: Cron trigger in rules is more than 20 minutes delayed
body:
<!-- Provide a general summary of the issue in the *Title* above -->
Using openHAB 4.1.0. 
A Rule is triggered by cron `cronExpression: 0 0 9 ? * MON,TUE,WED,THU,FRI *`. But the rule action runs allways more than 20 minutes delayed.

I already tried this, without success:
- Restart of ohenhab service
- Restart of OS (ubuntu)
- Deactivate for some minutes and activate the rule
- Shell command "date" shows correct time
- Using datetime in scripts (in OH rules) shows the correct time.
- Timezone in OpenHab and in OS is correct.

In the community I found a similar problem: https://community.openhab.org/t/everything-happens-51-minutes-too-late/132112
But there they solved the problem by a restart, which dit not work for me.

Does OH run an own clock? 

## Expected Behavior
The rule actions should be triggered in the same minute of the cron trigger



<!-- If you're suggesting a change/improvement, tell us how it should work -->

## Current Behavior
Example rule:
````
...
triggers:
  - id: "1"
    configuration:
      cronExpression: 0 0 9 ? * MON,TUE,WED,THU,FRI *
    type: timer.GenericCronTrigger
conditions: []
actions:
  - inputs: {}
    id: "2"
    configuration:
      command: ON
      itemName: MQTTLED03_LED03onoff
    type: core.ItemCommandAction
...
````

````
2023-12-14 09:24:34.188 [INFO ] [openhab.event.ItemCommandEvent      ] - Item 'MQTTLED03_LED03onoff' received command ON
````

Expected:
The event should be triggered at 9:00, not at 9:24

<!-- If describing a bug, tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior -->
<!-- Include related log information (preferably debug level) and related configs -->
<!-- Use a file attachment for log and config information longer than a few lines -->
<!-- Enclose multi-line log/code snippets with ``` on new lines for proper formatting -->
<!-- If suggesting a change/improvement, explain the difference from current behavior -->
<!-- For improvements, discuss at community.openhab.org first and include link to topic -->

## Possible Solution
If OH uses an own clock, it should be synchonized with the OS clock.

## Steps to Reproduce (for Bugs)
On my system I can reproduce it with different cron and time triggers.
On a clean new OH installation, the bug would probably be not reprducable.

## Context
I am using OH since version 3.0.0 and updated it several times by ````sudo apt-get upgrade````.
In former times I did not have the time delay.


## Your Environment
* Version used: openHAB 4.1.0.
* Environment name and version: Chrome Browser 
* Operating System and version: Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS (GNU/Linux 5.15.0-91-generic x86_64), which runs on a virtual machine (virtualbox)

It doesn't use it's own clock and does use the system clock. It does it's own timezone configuration but it uses the OS clock. 

Something else is going on. 

OH 4 is known to require more RAM than OH 3. Have you reached the limit of your machine? Check the system settings, in particular the system load, available memory, and swap. If the load is high, swap is in use and/or available memory is low, you might have outgrown your machine.

I do not think the load is the problem:

- 24 minutes

A load average above 1 is concerning. It means at any given time over the past 15 minutes you've always had at least one process stuck waiting around for resources.

The fact that you are suing *any* swap at all and your free memory being really low points to this machine being over allocated and it's run out of RAM. 

> Other triggers (e.g. switches) are working directly.

If those are still in RAM and haven't been swapped out that's to be expected. The parts of RAM that have been accessed the longest ago are the parts that get swapped out first. Cron triggered rules don't need to subscribe to the event bus so those parts of RAM get accessed less frequently and therefore are more likely to be swapped out.

> During this long time is allways a slot with CPU load less than 5%.

It's not CPU constrained. It's RAM constrained. The load shows you always have at least one process waiting around for some bit of data to be restored to RAM from SWAP (which means taking some other chunk of data out of RAM and writing it to the file system at slow USB speeds, and then reading the needed chunk of data from the file system at USB speeds back into RAM) so your overall CPU utilization is going to be very low. It's stuck waiting around for two file system operations to complete before it can process any instructions for that process.

The greater your system load, the *less* your CPU will be able to run.

Based on that top command, it's very clear to me that the problem is RAM

I#m not sure whether my issue is related to yours, but I'm facing also problems with different times and deviations since introduction of oh4. [https://github.com/openhab/openhab-js/issues/299].

As a workaround i reload all rules/scripts with time constraints at night by script. 

o.

> A load average above 1 is concerning. It means at any given time over the past 15 minutes you've always had at least one process stuck waiting around for resources.

@rkoshak Thank you for this. I have now increased the CPU of the virtual machine from 1 to 2 kernels. 
Now the constant delay is fixed (actually the delay is now 1 minute, which is OK for me).

> The fact that you are suing any swap at all and your free memory being really low points to this machine being over allocated and it's run out of RAM.

Additionally I increased the RAM size from 2GB to 4GB and the delay is now less than 1 second.

It would be nice to find the minimum system requirement somewhere in the documentation.
The only section I found is on the welcome page  [While You Are Getting Started](https://www.openhab.org/docs/#while-you-are-getting-started): 

"_If you have no strong preference, get a Raspberry Pi 4 with 2 GB and a 16 GB SD card and install [openHABian](https://www.openhab.org/docs/installation/openhabian.html) for the best experience._"

I would expect the system requirement here: [openHAB on Linux: Meeting the Requirements](https://www.openhab.org/docs/installation/linux.html#meeting-the-requirements)

It would be nice to have an update in the documentation, for all the others who run into the same problem.
Thank you again for your help.

It's still under investigation. And there is debate. an average OH instance by itself runs just fine on an RPi 3. It's only when you add third party stuff like Mosquitto, InfluxDB, Frontail, NodeRed, zigbee2mqtt, etc. that tracks arise.

Does that mean an RPi 3 isn't enough to run OH?
@openhab/core-maintainers : can be closed, the problem was a lack of RAM which was then resolved by the user.

title: L4D2server script fails to find lock file
body:
Background

Testing your latest L4D2server script on two different VMs, one with a fresh install of **Ubuntu Server 14.04.2 LTS** and the other with a fresh install of **Debian 8 Jessie amd64.** All required 32-bit libraries and other packages were installed per your instructions at: http://danielgibbs.co.uk/lgsm/l4d2server/ L4D2server script completes the Initial game server installation without issue. Script functions (start, stop, restart, update, validate, etc.) all work correctly. Automated monitoring setup by downloading `gsquery.py` (by script during initial installation) and a new cron job created for 3 minute checks: `*/3 * * * * /home/patriot/gameservers/l4d2server monitor > /dev/null 2>&1` Issuing the command `./l4d2server start` the game server starts correctly without issue and a `.l4d2-server.lock` file is created in the same directory where the script and `gsquery.py` exist.

Issue

The `l4d2-server-script.log` located in `/home/patriot/gameservers/log/script` has these entries: Mar 17 13:21:01 l4d2-server: Monitor: ubuntu test Mar 17 13:21:02 l4d2-server: Monitor: Disabled: No lock file found Mar 17 13:24:01 l4d2-server: Monitor: ubuntu test Mar 17 13:24:02 l4d2-server: Monitor: Disabled: No lock file found and yet **the lock file clearly exists.** Debian 8 produces the same results in its script log.

Result

Because the script fails to find the `.l4d2-server.lock` file, **the game server monitoring process does not work** and if the game server is forced to crash with the rcon command `quit`, **the server is not restarted by the cron job.** This is the only issue I've found with your latest script. If you are able to resolve it the script seems very solid. Thank you for all of your hard work developing these scripts and for making them available to the community free of charge. Cheers, Patriot

Also to clarify here since you closed where I was talking about it @DanVanAtta   Any root can be changed at the linode level  quite easily on a server reboot once securely logged into linode.  So I guess your saying the 5 of us are a security issue?

@RoiEXLab root login with password is not quite the same as the root account not having a password. Once logged into a machine, one can `su` and use password. Having an oddball server not have keys managed the same way, or to get updates, adds to our work (otherwise it would be just one of N machines, with an application that is still hand-managed; thinking back to TripleA's system infrastructure history, where updated jar files were dropped in from folders created years ago, with no information beyond that, I'm eager to see us automate all of this so we can invest minimal time to sys-admin and focus on other priorities)

title: Cron Backfill example doesn't work
body:
## Summary

I was trying a functionality that is required for our use case: cron backfill. I took the examples from this page : https://argoproj.github.io/argo/cron-backfill/, but unfortunately it doesn't work. 

Here is the complete file
```
# This is an example of back-filling day for a daily cron workflow.
# See ../docs/cron-backfill.md
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: WorkflowTemplate
metadata:
  name: job
spec:
  arguments:
    parameters:
      - name: date
  templates:
    - name: main
      inputs:
        parameters:
          - name: date
            value: "{{inputs.parameters.date}}"
            # use "yesterday" is a magic value to tell the script it needs to determine the day to run
            default: yesterday
      script:
        image: docker/whalesay:latest
        command:
          - sh
        source: |
          date="{{inputs.parameters.date}}"
          if [ $date = yesterday ]; then
            date=$(date -d yesterday +%Y-%m-%d)
          fi
          echo "run for $date"
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: CronWorkflow
metadata:
  name: daily-job
spec:
  # run daily at 2am
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  workflowSpec:
    workflowTemplateRef:
      name: job
---
# This version will create jobs as fast as it can - not waiting for
# each to complete. Use this when you really need each workflow separate.
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: backfill-v1
spec:
  entrypoint: main
  # the backfill must use a service account which can create workflows
  # you should not - despite this example - use "argo-server"
  serviceAccountName: argo-server
  templates:
    - name: main
      steps:
        - - name: day
            template: create-job
            arguments:
              parameters:
                - name: date
                  value: "{{item}}"
            withSequence:
              # run for the 19th to the 21st
              start: "19"
              end: "21"
              format: "2020-05-%02X"
    - # this template creates each workflow
      name: create-job
      inputs:
        parameters:
          - name: date
      resource:
        action: apply
        manifest: |
          apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
          kind: Workflow
          metadata:
            # using a name based on the date prevents re-creating resources,
            # making this more robust
            name: job-{{inputs.parameters.date}}
          spec:
            entrypoint: main
            templates:
              - name: main
                steps:
                  - - name: start-job
                      arguments:
                        parameters:
                          - name: date
                            value: "{{inputs.parameters.date}}"
                      templateRef:
                        name: job
                        template: main
---
# This version creates each job as part of the workflow, and limits concurrent jobs using
# `spec.parallelism`
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: backfill-v2
spec:
  entrypoint: main
  # limit to one job at a time
  parallelism: 1
  templates:
    - name: main
      steps:
        - - name: create-job
            templateRef:
              name: job
              template: main
            arguments:
              parameters:
                - name: date
                  value: "{{item}}"
            withSequence:
              # run for the 19th to the 21st
              start: "19"
              end: "21"
              format: "2020-05-%02X"
```

When I try to submit the WorkflowTemplate, I get this error :
```spec.arguments.date.value is required```


When I try to submit the cron workflow, it throws the following error:
```Invalid CronWorkflow: metadata.namespace cannot be blank```
I then add a namespace to it, but I get the following error :

comments.body:
The patch fixes the issue on master:

```
diff --git a/examples/cron-backfill.yaml b/examples/cron-backfill.yaml
index 5f35e211..15982981 100644
--- a/examples/cron-backfill.yaml
+++ b/examples/cron-backfill.yaml
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@ spec:

+        value: yesterday

@@ -35,6 +36,7 @@ spec:

```

But this used to work - so what changed?

body:
### Prerequisites

### Describe the bug and add attachments

Hi,
The gsitemap module, ver 4.4.0, installed on a PS 8.1.4. It works fine when I launch the url directly (https://my-domaine/gsitemap/cron?toke,n=xxxxxxx).
But it doesn't work as cron task, the server send me a mail error with "No such file or directory" and the sitemap is not created.
I have this issue on all my recent website.

DO you have an idea ? If I remember, it was possible to create a script to lanch the url and we have to add this script as cron. But I dont retrieve how to do.

THanks a lot

### Expected behavior

RTo renew the sitemap with the cron

### Steps to reproduce

Go to the server
Add a cron
Enter 0 0 * * * https://www.my_domain.com/module/gsitemap/cron?token=335b216e31&id_shop=1

When the task is launched manually by copy/paste the link in the browser, the sitemap is updated

### PrestaShop version(s) where the bug happened

8.1.4

### PHP version(s) where the bug happened

7.4

### If your bug is related to a module, specify its name and its version

gsitemap v.4.4.0

### Your company or customer's name goes here (if applicable).

_No response_

comments.body:
Hello @sirius82,

Thanks for reporting this issue!
Ping @PrestaShop/prestashop-core-developers : Could someone please try to reproduce the issue, it's too technical!

title: IHMValidation update cron job doesn't work on production instance
body:
Apparently, after the re-deployment of the production instance, IHMValidation code wasn't updated.

 `/root/ihm_validation_checkout.sh` (the update script) had the right tag  "20240320"
but the code wasn't updated after re-deployment and was showing "20240315" tag. 

After i called it manually, the correct revision was pulled to the server.

comments.body:
@aozalevsky The `production` is`NOT` supposed to do automatically updates like the `dev` that has `crontab` scripts for the daily updates.

The `production` works with tags.
Each time a new `tag` is provided, we run manually the updates.

You will see on the `/root` directory:
 - the `www-update.sh` script that has tags for `derivapy`, `pdb` backend, `python_ihm` and `ihm_validation`
 - the `ihm_validation_checkout.sh` script (a subset of the `www-update.sh` script) that has tag just for `ihm_validation`

In the case a new tag is provided for `derivapy`, `pdb` backend, `python_ihm` or `ihm_validation`, the updated `www-update.sh` script will be run manually.

In the case a new tag is provided just for the `ihm_validation`, the updated `ihm_validation_checkout.sh` script will be run manually.
@svoinea The problem is that the tag from `/root/ihm_validation_checkout.sh` wasn't pulled during the redeployment from scratch.

@aozalevsky The explanation is that for the redeployment from scratch, I was running `/root/www-update.sh` that had:
```
    "python_ihm_validation 20240315"
```
I should have updated the tag before running it.

title: Page cache not set if requested via HTTP HEAD
body:
Steps to reproduce:
- Enable the page cache.
- Clear all caches.
- From the command line, run: `curl http://backdrop.dev/ --head`. You should get a response like this:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Thu, 21 Apr 2016 22:19:41 GMT
Server: Apache
X-Powered-By: PHP/5.3.29
X-Backdrop-Cache: MISS
Expires: Sun, 19 Nov 1978 05:00:00 GMT
Last-Modified: Thu, 21 Apr 2016 22:19:41 +0000
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
ETag: 1461277181
Content-Language: en
X-Generator: Backdrop CMS 1 (http://backdropcms.org)
Connection: close
Vary: Cookie
Content-Length: 6425
Content-Range: 0-6424/6425
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
```
- Check the database, the `cache_page` table is still empty for the homepage.
- You can run `curl http://backdrop.dev/ --head` again as many times as you want, but `X-Backdrop-Cache: MISS` will always be set. No entry is being saved in the database.

**Cause:**

I haven't been able to find much documentation on this behavior other than an ancient mailing list reference, but it appears to be a behavior of Apache and mod_php. If a `HEAD` request is performed, as soon as a string is printed to the page, the execution of PHP is immediately ended. This makes things like our background-processing (cron jobs) not work on HEAD requests. It also prevents the saving of the page cache, because the page is printed first, then saved to the database after being delivered. If PHP is short-circuited when printing content, then the cache never gets set.

**Solution:**

Just don't print anything out on HTTP HEAD requests. This will keep Apache from terminating PHP early, because it will run until completion in the event that more headers might be set.

comments.body: PR filed at https://github.com/backdrop/backdrop/pull/1329 fixes this and adds a new page cache test.

I'm having a bit of trouble figuring out why my new test is failing. It only fails on PHP 5.3 in Travis. PHP 7 passes every time, as does PHP 5.3 on my localhost. There must be something I'm missing yet. But it is nice that this would seem to reveal there's another situation in which HEAD requests aren't setting the page cache properly.

I found that calling `flush()` on some versions of PHP also aborts `HEAD` requests, so we need to skip the flush call (forgoing background processing) if dealing with a HEAD request. Updated PR at https://github.com/backdrop/backdrop/pull/1329
Merged in https://github.com/backdrop/backdrop/pull/1329 that expands test coverage and fixes this particular issue with HEAD requests and the page cache. Merged into 1.x and 1.3.x.

title: Add automatic background job runs to Docker containers
body:
The application can preemptively expire and clean up pushes.  This is done daily on pwpush.com in a hacky automated fashion.

We can add the automated run of these tasks by adding cron to the Docker containers and using the [whenever](https://github.com/javan/whenever) gem to schedule the daily task.

This means the zfs command isnt in the PATH during the crontab execution.

Usually you can put something like PATH=$PATH:/usr/bin in front of the command. 

To find out the path of a command use:
```
which zfs
```

Also you can add 2>&1 to the command to see the actual errors as well, in your crontab:
```
zfs-autobackup .... 2>&1
```

If someone is going to the trouble of using Remote SSH in VS Code (as opposed to just using `ssh` from a terminal outside VS Code), then I _presume_ they'd be happy that VS Code is the default editor (as opposed to e.g. `nano` in the terminal window)?

comments.body:
I wanted to share a possible solution for the meanwhile. Add this to your `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc` etc:

```sh
if [ "$VSCODE_INJECTION" = "1" ]; then
    export EDITOR="code --wait"
fi
```

I believe @RAnders00 's workaround is the best solution, as it's straightforward and unopinionated.  I actually do think some folks like using their remote's default terminal editor alongside VS Code.  Please feel free to share your thoughts with me if you think strongly otherwise
I documented how to set this up in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/pull/7865

title: Add random sleep inside `certbot renew`
body:
If you use a packaged certbot, it comes with a crontab that includes a random sleep. However, a lot of people are configuring their own crontabs, either with certbot or certbot-auto. They usually run at midnight or the top of some other hour. These create very significant traffic spikes to Let's Encrypt.

I'd like Certbot to build in a random sleep interval when run with `renew`. Even an interval with a min of 1 minute and a max of 4 minutes would probably help a lot, though longer is better. I think there's no need to coordinate with the packaged sleep; if we have one external sleep and one internal sleep, that's fine.

@ohemorange points out that we need to make sure this runs before the hooks, so people with hooks that take down their web server don't have unnecessarily long outages.

Also, if we want to get fancy, we could insert the random sleep only when not being run from a terminal.

comments.body: @jsha, do you have some log data indicating what fraction of the load spikes are attributable to Certbot as opposed to other clients? What does the top-of-the-hour-renewal client distribution look like?
I don't have it on hand, but I did some investigation a while ago, and found that it was pretty heavily Certbot. Emailing a few of the users, I found that they had all installed a crontab by hand.

> Also, if we want to get fancy, we could insert the random sleep only when not being run from a terminal.

This is evidently as easy as

`if os.isatty(0):`

I tried

```
#!/usr/bin/env python

import os

open("/tmp/log", "w").write(str(os.isatty(0)) + "\n")
```

Running this program from the command line produced a `/tmp/log` containing the string `True`; creating a crontab to run it caused the contents to change to `False` as soon as the job had run.
@ohemorange tells me we already do this detection somewhere; we should reuse that.

I think it's in `log.py` and `reporter.py` where we check `sys.stderr.isatty()` and `sys.stdout.isatty()`, but the result isn't necessarily exported in a convenient way for other code to use. However, we could use exactly the same method that those tests use.

OK, I have a proof of concept of this. Two other questions:

* should we announce in the logs that this sleep is happening?
* should OS packagers disable this feature in their OS packages so that they don't have the duplicative sleeps?

> should we announce in the logs that this sleep is happening?

Yes.

> should OS packagers disable this feature in their OS packages so that they don't have the duplicative sleeps?

No. The OS package have much longer sleeps than we are likely to want to put inside Certbot itself, and a longer max sleep time is better (distributes traffic over a wider range of times). If the OS crontab sleeps, and Certbot also sleeps, that's no problem.
@jsha when you messaged the people, did you happen to confirm that they're definitely putting `certbot renew` inside their crontab, and not a different subcommand like `certonly`?

comments.body:
Guess that is not a borg problem, but caused by a different environment, like e.g.:
- different shell causing different behaviour relating to tilde expansion, quoting and escaping?
- different environment variables? like e.g. $HOME.

borg does **not** check whether it is run from cron or not, so if it is invoked with the same cli args and the same env vars, it would behave the same.

Within both contexts, the --exclude arguments work as expected, but these pattern ones seem to be ignored in the cronjob context.

I was unable to figure out how to use the tilde with the --pattern and I find the documentation around --pattern to be quite confusing, making me have to guess and go through trial and error to know if I have the syntax correct.

This command is ran in a shell script in both manual and cronjob contexts with the bash environment set. And while I know cronjob still has less variables set, I don't see why it would be ignoring that last pattern when it would respect the --exclude equivalent. `-e /Users/soul/Library`.

IIRC, borg does nothing with the tilde.

Usually, tilde expansion is the task of the shell.
Even a pattern like this `--pattern="-**/Library"` seems to work when I manually do it, but doesn't when tried via crontab.

I figured out what the problem was. `--pattern="-**/Library"` was giving the desired result, as so was `--pattern=-/Users/soul/Library`. I was just mistaking errors from it trying to access areas it can't in a crontab due to lack of permissions, with it trying to backup those areas. 

I settled on using `--pattern="-$HOME/Library"` as the tilde wasn't working with a `--pattern`.

Edit: I wish there was a way to include directories without having it go recursively in other sub directories that it should know aren't needed.

I've figured out that this argument `-e 're:^Users/soul/Library/(?!Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs|CloudStorage).+$'` works a lot better although a bit harder to read. It also seems to not go down these other subdirectories throwing all sorts of errors.

comments.body: Looks like this change was introduced in 2.12 according to https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/37355 (and PR https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/73591). I did not experience this issue using 2.11.x

Changing the `ubuntu2004cis_aide_cron.cron_file` variable to create a new `/etc/cron.d/aide` file rather than modify `/etc/crontab` resolves this issue.

```yml
- name: harden server to CIS benchmarks
  ansible.builtin.import_role:
    name: florianutz.ubuntu2004_cis
  vars:
    ubuntu2004cis_aide_cron:
      cron_user: root
      cron_file: aide
      aide_job: '/usr/bin/aide.wrapper --config /etc/aide/aide.conf --check'
      aide_minute: 0
      aide_hour: 5
      aide_day: '*'
      aide_month: '*'
      aide_weekday: '*'
```
I hit this as well, is this going to be merged as a fix?

I'm happy to submit a PR, but I'm not sure if this change is compatible with `ansible` versions < `2.12`. I had a tough time finding `ansible` docs for a specific version other than the [latest](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/cron_module.html#parameter-cron_file). title: Fails with Ansible 5
body:
First of all: Thanks a lot for creating this awesome role!

Unfortunately it doesn't work for me. As far as I can tell, ansible deprecated the use of /etc/crontab for managing cronjob.

Here are my vars:
```yaml
restic_create_schedule: true
restic_schedule_type: systemd
restic_repos:
  minio:
    location: s3:https://example.com/example
    password: "{{ restic_password }}"
    init: true
    aws_access_key: "{{ aws_access_key }}"
    aws_secret_access_key: "{{ aws_secret_access_key }}"
restic_backups:
  example:
    name: example-db
    repo: minio
    stdin: true
    stdin_cmd: docker exec example-postgres pg_dumpall -U postgres
    stdin_filename: postgres_dump.sql
    scheduled: true
    schedule_oncalendar: '*-*-* 01:00:00'
```

When running the playbook it wants to cleanup old crontab entries which fails, since it cannot change /etc/crontab files anymore.

Log:
```text
TASK [do1jlr.restic : delete old cronjob entry if available] ***********************************************************************************************************************************************
failed: [] (item={'name': 'example-db', 'repo': 'minio', 'stdin': True, 'stdin_cmd': 'docker exec example-postgres pg_dumpall -U postgres', 'stdin_filename': 'postgres_dump.sql', 'scheduled': True, 'schedule_oncalendar': '*-*-* 01:00:00'}) => {"ansible_loop_var": "item", "changed": false, "item": {"name": "example-db", "repo": "minio", "schedule_oncalendar": "*-*-* 01:00:00", "scheduled": true, "stdin": true, "stdin_cmd": "docker exec example-postgres pg_dumpall -U postgres", "stdin_filename": "postgres_dump.sql"}, "msg": "Will not manage /etc/crontab via cron_file, see documentation."}
```

Since it "failed" to create a systemd timer, the role then wants to create a cronjob, which also fails for the same reason.

I think you have to remove or change the `cron_file` value [here](https://github.com/roles-ansible/ansible_role_restic/blob/e614bdc66180692ee29906502514ba6349675949/tasks/schedule.yml#L83).

Thanks for having a look at it!

Me neither. I guess all you have to do is to omit the `cron_file` all together. It should then create the cronjob in root crontab. But this will cause a breaking change since Ansible will create a second cronjob for every backup task. Just so you know :)

title: acme.sh should provide a username in crontab entry
body:
When installing the cronjob, acme.sh [generates](https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh/blob/master/acme.sh#L5928) /etc/cron.d/acme.sh with:

crond needs to know what user to run acme.sh as. The error goes away when fixing the crontab entry:

title: Lack of minute should not pass the validation

comments.body: I've stumbled on this too. Similarly, expressions such as just `1` or `1 2` are considered valid while e.g. https://crontab.guru/ considers them invalid.

Currently, [validation](https://github.com/harrisiirak/cron-parser/blob/master/lib/expression.js#L846-L863) of the input expression is rather lax, and if there isn't value specified for the field, it fills it with wildcard.

Throwing an error probably would make more sense indeed. Not sure if somebody out there is relying on this "undocumented feature", but changing it to throw an error should be rather trivial.
Maybe it's a good idea to be part of `parseExpression` function option? To determine wheither there should be filled with wildcard

Since v5, the `strict` option enforces this: `parseExpression('20 15 * *', { strict: true })` throws `Invalid cron expression, expected 6 fields`. Note that strict mode requires all 6 fields, so seconds must be explicit (`0 20 15 * * *`). The default behavior still fills missing fields for backwards compatibility.
Closing this for now in favour of my last [comment](https://github.com/harrisiirak/cron-parser/issues/244#issuecomment-5160170502).

title: Export downloads cleaned before they ought to be
body:
EM at CA State Lib is getting a 500 error trying to download an export she did 4 days ago on the 1st.  

Looking at [the download record](https://fromthepage.com/bulk_export/6220) the processing log has been cleaned, which implies that the export zip file has also been cleaned.

The [rake file for cleaning up exports](https://github.com/benwbrum/fromthepage/blob/bc39845853452e10de1eab504e25f21d8fb364f0/lib/tasks/bulk_export.rake#L5) is passed an argument of 7 days when the task runs in the crontab.  I double checked the logic, and that's what this code does.

The cron job that calls the rake task 
`00 5 * * * /bin/bash -l -c 'cd /home/fromthepage/deployment/current && RAILS_ENV=production bundle exec rake fromthepage:clean_bulk_exports[7] >> /tmp/cron_log_file7 2>&1'`

The code that "unlinks" (not actually deleting??) the export file:
https://github.com/benwbrum/fromthepage/blob/development/app/models/bulk_export.rb#L124

Looking at the /tmp directory, there are no downloads there:

> fromthepage@fromthepage:/tmp/fromthepage_exports$ pwd
> /tmp/fromthepage_exports
> fromthepage@fromthepage:/tmp/fromthepage_exports$ ls
> fromthepage@fromthepage:/tmp/fromthepage_exports$ 

Which is really weird because [an export that ran today is downloadable](https://fromthepage.com/bulk_export/6227) and says it's in that (empty) directory.  (So I"m thinking the empty /tmp directory is a red herring.)

It looks like exports run on August 2nd are also cleaned.  Exports run on August 3rd are not.

So why is the exports being if they are older than 3 days, rather than 7?

comments.body:
We've done some more research on this and are stumped.  The strange thing is that, in production the rails console writes to `/tmp/fromthepage_exports` and we can see the outputs on the filesystem.  However, the web app does does not appear to write any files which are visible, even though it can display their results.

So running an export from the UI shows https://fromthepage.com/bulk_export/7007 including the log file
```


```

This should be pulled from a log file [see source](https://github.com/benwbrum/fromthepage/blob/337b29aea556b20056fbf7a46e047da7757b95cb/app/models/bulk_export.rb#L145) streamed from a syscall to a rake task
```
I, [2024-10-22T16:51:17.692338 #2021585]  INFO -- : nice -n 10 /usr/bin/env rake fromthepage:process_bulk_export[7007]  --trace >> /tmp/fromthepage_exports/rake_bulk_export_7007.log 2>&1 &
```

However, there is nothing in the tmp directory:
```
fromthepage@fromthepage:~/deployment/current$ ls /tmp/fromthepage_exports/
fromthepage@fromthepage:~/deployment/current$ 
```
So why is our application able to write and see files that we cannot?

This happened again this week.  [This export](https://fromthepage.com/bulk_export/11815) was started on Friday, Feb 13.  It completed successfully.  When they went to download it on Monday the 16th they received a 500 error.  I looked today on the 17th on the tmp file is gone and I also get a 500 error.  

I'm going to bump this up in priority.  I feel like @WillNigel23 had a theory on why this might be happening as well.  (I think his theory was related to deployments -- the last deployment was on 2/10:  current -> /home/fromthepage/deployment/releases/20260210232612
But maybe app restarts?  But we do an app restart every 5 minutes, so that would affect everything:
*/5 * * * * /bin/bash -l -c 'touch /home/fromthepage/deployment/current/tmp/restart.txt'

apache restarts?  I do not believe we did one on Friday, Saturday, Sunday or Monday / the last 4 days.  @benwbrum did you happen to do an apache restart this weekend?

My working theory is that the export finished successfully, users went ahead to download it, but since we are saving it in a temp dir, it's gone by the time they wanted to download the file. I'm not sure how temp files are cleaned (I'm certain restarts wipe out the temp dir, but unsure if there are any other processes that does so)

I think it's in our best interest here to:
1. Store the export file somewhere other than temp dir
2. Add boolean field to indicate if an export has been `downloaded` at least once
3. Add recurring job of deleting export files that are already downloaded or too old

I like the idea of storing somewhere other than the temp directory.
I don't think we need #2, as long as we implement a reasonable (2 weeks) #3.

That makes sense. 

Although should we add a new status to bulk export, probably `archived` so we don't confuse users when they access the downloads late.
I think we already have a 'cleaned' status, which I prefer over 'archived' which implies it's still around (especially to archivists!).

title: Snapshot scheduling
body:
Hello

Is it possible to implement some extra snapshot feature (ex:  TTL on snapshot)  in order to have them automatically created and deleted when TTL expired.

For the moment i have to use "zfSnap" in crontab; a tool which add a TTL to snapshot and automatically delete the snapshot when TTL is expired.

     # Snap LXC
     0 * * * * /infra/tools/lxd_snap.sh > /tmp/cron_lxd_snap.log 2>&1

basically, it runs : 
/usr/sbin/zfSnap -s -z -a 24h -r zdata/lxd/containers

another cron at midnight to delete old snap  : /usr/sbin/zfSnap -d -s -S

Results is to have a snap per hour : 

    root@inxovh-hy002 (node2):~# ls -la /var/lib/lxd/containers/inxovh-adm001.zfs/.zfs/snapshot/
    total 0
    dr-xr-xr-x 2 root root 2 Nov 14 11:11 .
    dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov  7 20:50 ..
    dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov 14 11:57 2016-11-14_10.45.00--24h
    dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov 14 11:57 2016-11-14_10.46.00--1w
    dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov 14 11:57 2016-11-14_11.00.00--24h
    dr-xr-xr-x 1 root root 0 Nov 14 11:57 2016-11-14_11.11.00--24h

So, that means, snapshot with 24h TTL will be deleted tomorrow and the one with "1w" will be deleted in 7 days.

Using snapshot is useful *not to restore an entire container* (it almost never happens) but to restaure specific files for any reason (- bad modification, deleted by error; wrong update after a patch etc).

So, would it be possible to add a snapshot feature which integrates:

- a scheduler to plan automatic snapshot for containers
- a TTL for each snapshot
- a scheduler to plan automatic remove of old snapshot according to its TTL
- a way to restore specific files without having to to to .zfs/snapshots/files  : 

lxc snapshot <container_name> <frequency> <TTL>

ex:

    lxc snapshot inxovh-adm001  "0 * * * *" 24h
    => will add scheduler to do an hourly snap with 24h TTL for container named  inxovh-adm001 

    lxc snapshot inxovh-adm001  "0 23 * * 7" 1w
    => will add scheduler to do a snap every sunday at 23h00 for container named inxovh-adm001


Then for restore : 

    lxc restore <container_name>  <path_file_to_restore> [<path_dest>]  [<date_snapshot>]

Usage example:
                    
     lxc restore inxovh-adm001 /etc/hosts
    => it will restore the file /etc/hosts from the LAST snap

     lxc restore inxovh-adm001 /etc/hosts 2016-11-14_11.11.00
    => it will restore the file /etc/hosts from snap at the date 2016-11-14_11.11.00

    lxc restore inxovh-adm001 /etc/network/interfaces /tmp/interfaces  2016-11-12_11.11.00
    => it will restore the file /etc/hosts from snap at the date 2016-11-12_11.11.00 and copy it in /tmp/interfaces instead of original path.

This is just a thought but would add lot of value in our day to day usage of LXD.

Thanks
Regards
nico

title: ZFS Initialize works only once
body:
OS: Zorin OS 16.2-r1 (Ubuntu derivative)
Kernel: 5.15.0-57-generic #63~20.04.1-Ubuntu SMP Wed Nov 30 13:40:16 UTC 2022
Machine: HP 17-cp1035cl, 12 GB RAM, 1 TB spinning rust internal drive, ZFS (rpool, bpool) in mirrored rpool setup with 2 (mirrored) SLOG drives

Ok, so I've got this little code blurb set up as a keyboard shortcut (Super+F):
gnome-terminal -- /bin/sh -c 'set zfs:zfs_initialize_value=0; sudo zpool initialize bpool d7335f16-9bd1-1c4d-88b9-e952441dd227; sudo zpool initialize rpool 965d0a40-cce9-664d-8f4a-04c8075238c4 b34bba5d-f7ed-4d3e-95b5-47fd750e05f6 1a7428f8-4950-c248-b947-d8b817a0cd5a b5fd0c2c-0f02-9942-8576-d7b0b851fef1; while sudo zpool status | grep "initializing" > /dev/null; do clear; sudo zpool status -Td; sleep 2; done; clear; sudo zpool status -Td; sleep 15'

It sets the value used by zfs_initialize from '0xdeadbeefdeadbeef' to '0', then initializes all the rpool drives. The idea is to zero unused (free) space on the drives so that backing up the drive to an .img file, then compressing that file, results in a very small .img.7z file (the 1 TB main drive backup compressed to a 2.8 GB file, whereas without zero'ing sectors, it compressed to a 8.4 GB file).

It can also be used when running VMs, to reduce the size of the VMs by zeroing previously-used drive sectors, although I don't use it for that.

It can also be used for security purposes, to ensure sensitive data that resides on previously-used sectors is zero'd, although I don't use it for that.

I had to include the PARTUUID of each drive because otherwise zpool initialize throws the error: "Cannot initialize rpool. 'hole' device not available." That's apparently a bug, not just for zpool initialize.

The problem:
sudo zpool initialize only works the first time. After that, it ends very quickly and doesn't zero free space. I believe this is because zpool initialize keeps a record of its progress, then when it's finished, it doesn't discard this data, so on subsequent runs it believes it's already finished.

I can detach then reattach each drive in rpool (allowing the pool to resilver, then performing a scrub for each drive detached and reattached), and zpool initialize will again work as desired... bolstering the notion that zpool initialize is keeping a record of its progress and not discarding it after its first run.

We have here an excellent opportunity to solve a long-standing issue... that of zero'ing previously-used drive sectors. All we have to do is figure out how to discard the progress data that zpool initialize keeps.

So... I ask the developers of OpenZFS: where is that data and how do we delete it? Can a flag be programmed into zpool initialize such that we can delete that data when we run zpool initialize?

Of course, ideally, it would keep track of the sectors that are data-occupied, keep track of the sectors it's already zero'd, then when run from a cron job, only zero newly-unused sectors.

comments.body:
I've created a script that allows zpool initialize to work repeatedly, rather than just once... it detaches one drive from the mirror, reattaches it, does the resilver and scrub, then detaches the other drive from the mirror, reattaches it, does the resilver and scrub, does the initialize on the rpool, then turns off the swap partition, zeros the sectors on it, and reestablishes the swap partition with the same UUID (so I don't have to mess with fstab each time I run the script).

https://forum.zorin.com/t/zfs-zero-drives-to-get-better-backup-img-file-compression-while-running-linux/24086/3

Then I boot into the Zorin OS Boot USB stick and use a script I created (dd chained to 7z) to back up the internal drive to a .img.7z file.

It works, I just did the entire procedure, and the .img.7z file was 2.9 GB for a 1 TB drive image (and that after I'd uninstalled GIMP, installed another simpler graphics program, did system updates, updated grub via sudo apt dist-upgrade, and added the Zorin OS Boot USB stick to the grub menu... so with the ZFS CoW, there were definitely sectors that had data on them that were now unused).

This is covered by e34e15ed6 "Add the ability to uninitialize" (#14873), available since 2.2.0. Running `zpool initialize -u <pool>` clears the previous initialize state, and a later `zpool initialize` writes all free space again.

Feel free to reopen if I missed something.

When run with the `--vlan` option, `navtopology` will analyze VLAN topologies, and ends the analysis by deleting from the database all VLAN entries that seems to have gone unused. The list of VLAN records being deleted is logged at the *INFO* level.

comments.body: Easy to control for FileHandler, but StreamHandler is a rabbit-hole, see for instance: https://vstinner.github.io/python3-locales-encodings.html
I've not managed to trigger the bug for StreamHandler at all, and I have a test for FileHandler. Stay tuned.

I can't get the test to fail every time when it should.

What's probably happening is this:

Works, should not raise exception, locale **C.UTF-8**:

```
import logging, locale
locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, 'C.UTF-8')
root = logging.getLogger('')
fh = logging.FileHandler('/tmp/blbl4')
root.addhandler(fh)
root.error('Blåbærsyltetøy')
```

Raises exception, and should do so, locale **C**:

```
import logging, locale
locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, 'C')
root = logging.getLogger('')
fh = logging.FileHandler('/tmp/blbl4')
root.addhandler(fh)
root.error('Blåbærsyltetøy')
```

Both locales seem to work for StreamHandler, though I assume piping such a stream would lead to problems.

The problem is, making a test that sets an ASCII locale and then calls NAV's `init_generic_logging` doesn't work, it always succeeds if the *test user*'s locale is UTF-8. I assume this is due to `logging` being a Borg/Singleton. The encoding is set the *first* time a filehandler is made, and you cannot control *when* a filehandler is made because it might happen if `logging.<somelevel>` is ever called *before* logging is explicitly setup, (because that runs `logging.basicLogging`), for instance in a 3rd party library.
I imagined the issue would be the encoding Python sets for `sys.stderr`,based on the environment, BEFORE any of your Python code runs?
I haven't been able to trigger this bug with StreamHandler (stderr).

The FileHandler-problem is trivially solved with 

```
fh = logging.FileHandler('/tmp/blbl4', encoding='utf-8')
```
So the bug is presumably fixed by #2133, but may require further work, re #2132

title: [BUG] `remove increments --older-than` returns an error when there is no increment to remove in v2.1.0a1
body:
## Bug summary

Using v2.1.0a1, calling *with the new or old interface*, removing increments with the `--older-than` option returns 1 (error) if there is no increment old enough to be removed.

## Version, Python, Operating System

```yaml
---
exec:
  api_version:
    actual: 0
    default: 200
    max: 201
    min: 200
  argv:
  - c:\Program Files\rdiff-backup\rdiff-backup.exe
  - info
  version: 2.1.0a1
python:
  executable: c:\Program Files\rdiff-backup\rdiff-backup.exe
  name: cpython
  version: 3.9.1
system:
  fs_encoding: utf-8
  platform: Windows-10-10.0.19041-SP0
...
```

## rdiff-backup call

```
"C:\Program Files\rdiff-backup-v210a1\rdiff-backup.exe" remove increments --older-than 3Y D:\  # returns 1
"C:\Program Files\rdiff-backup-v205\rdiff-backup.exe" --remove-older-than 3Y D:\  # returns 0
```

## What happened and what did you expect?

`rdiff-backup` v2.1.0a1 returns `1` while v2.0.5 returns `0`.

As a user, I would expect the command to return `0` (success) if it can access the backup directory and list its increments, meaning it runs without unexpected error, even if there is no matching increment to remove and it terminates without removing any.
This expectation seems consistent with how the `man` entry describes `rdiff-backup` return value:
````
If rdiff-backup finishes successfully, the exit status will be  0.   If
       there  is  an unrecoverable (critical) error, it will be non-zero (usu-
       ally 1, but don't depend on this  specific  value).   When  setting  up
       rdiff-backup  to  run  automatically (as from cron(8) or similar) it is
       probably a good idea to check the exit code.
````

Note that this "no matching increment found" case is different from the "specified increment not found" case of removing a given specific increment, where it does make sense to consider it an error if the increment doesn't exist.

## More information

My use case is running `rdiff-backup` in automated scripts and performing cleanup of old backups automatically.
The current behavior makes it impossible to check the exit code for potential execution error (e.g. "backup repository unaccessible") as suggested by the manual in such a use case.

comments.body: Well, this is disputable: you could have a typo in your script and never know that nothing is being done because the return code is 0. This said,  I'll stick to the behaviour of 2.0.5 by default. Thanks for reporting the issue.

To address all possibilities we would need 3 return values, like `grep` does:
- increments found and deleted without errors
- no increment found and no error
- unexpected error occurred.

As long as we have only two, they can only determinate whether increments were found and deleted successfully or not, or whether an error occurred or not.

To clarify why I argued for the second of these choices (especially wrt the goal for the exit status stated in the manual):
the issue of a typo for example is usually determined interactively or at the script-testing phase, during which the user can review the output and notice an unexpected "No increment removed" output. On the other hand, automatic / scheduled scripts run unattended and in this case it is more useful to know when an unexpected error, which should be manually checked and addressed, happened.
Otherwise, scripts have to either ignore the result, or add convoluted pre-checks to only run a remove command when matching increments are present.
I'm sure there are use cases for automatically determining whether any increment has been removed or not, but I would assume they are more limited and less common.

In any way, thanks for addressing the change of behavior.

I would personally close this ticket as "Won't do". Current behaviour is satisfiable. Return an error if nothing was done. Simiar to `rm invalid`.

The only useful case as stated is within a script and I would leave the script writer the responsibility to handle that scenario the way they want by ignoring the exitcode or parsing the stdout.

I could agree but for two reasons, I won't :grin: 

1. the behaviour isn't wanted, it came by chance, which probably means that something is wrong in the code, this should be addressed.
2. if rdiff-backup acted differently, we should stay consistent

title: Deprecation Warning "Using the last argument as keyword parameters is deprecated"
body:
In our codebase, we have Ruby 3 deprecation warnings enabled via:

```ruby
Warning[:deprecated] = true
```

When we run a cron job via `load_from_hash`:

```ruby
schedule_file = "config/schedule.yml"

if File.exist?(schedule_file) && Sidekiq.server?
  schedule_hash = YAML.load_file(schedule_file)
  Sidekiq::Cron::Job.load_from_hash schedule_hash
end
```

We always end up seeing a warning message:

```
/usr/local/bundle/gems/sidekiq-cron-1.10.1/lib/sidekiq/cron/job.rb:472: warning: Using the last argument as keyword parameters is deprecated; maybe ** should be added to the call
```

Is this a known issue with `sidekiq-cron` or has this been fixed in versions > 1.10.1?

comments.body:
Hello @jvanderen1 and thanks for reporting this warning. This is not tracked yet in any issue or PR, so feel free to send a patch! We'd be very happy to review it 🤝 

Btw, you can already remove this file now, as it will be automatically picked by the [gem itself](https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron/blob/master/lib/sidekiq/cron/schedule_loader.rb): https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron?tab=readme-ov-file#loading-jobs-from-schedule-file.

@markets Thank you for the suggestion! In the example above, I did omit some smaller details. For example, before we start any cronjobs, we actually delete any active one's first.

i.e.
```ruby
### First delete all jobs
Sidekiq::Cron::Job.all.each(&:destroy)

### Then load config/schedule.yml and restart
schedule_file = "config/schedule.yml"
if File.exist?(schedule_file) && Sidekiq.server?

  schedule_hash = YAML.load_file(schedule_file)
  Sidekiq::Cron::Job.load_from_hash schedule_hash
end
```

Is this necessary to do or will the gem automatically delete stale jobs when `require`d?

In the schedule loader we are using the bang suffixed methods:

https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron/blob/81268643b8fe4bb0a2197cb650b16a115a220c6f/lib/sidekiq/cron/schedule_loader.rb#L12

https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron/blob/81268643b8fe4bb0a2197cb650b16a115a220c6f/lib/sidekiq/cron/job.rb#L248-L249

Those methods☝️ clean up old jobs. So yes, you can delete your custom load file. I'd also recommend to upgrade to the last stable version: https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1120.
I went ahead and created https://github.com/sidekiq-cron/sidekiq-cron/pull/479. Thank you!

apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1

**Describe the user story**

As a developer working on a macOS computer, I want to ensure that all `node_module` folders created as part of the `pnpm install` process have the extended attribute `com.apple.metadata:com_apple_backup_excludeItem` set to `1` in the filesystem. This will allow me to **exclude these folders from backups** and avoid unnecessary duplication of data on my system.

When I run `pnpm install`, I expect that all `node_module` **folders created during the installation process** will have the `com.apple.metadata:com_apple_backup_excludeItem` attribute set to `1. This will ensure that these folders are excluded from backups and not included in any future system snapshots.

By default, macOS does not set this attribute on new folders, so I would like to request that pnpm include a feature that automatically sets this attribute on all node_module folders created during the pnpm install process. 
This will save me time and effort, as I will not have to manually set this attribute on each folder or manually initialize a process, and will ensure that my system backups are more efficient and streamlined.

Overall, adding this feature will help to further align pnpm with its philosophy of efficient and streamlined package management, while also providing a practical benefit to developers who use macOS and want to optimize their system backups.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

As I have no information on the percentage of user of `pnpm` using MacOS, I would suggest one of the following implementations:
1. Implement in core:
   * only add the extended attribute after the `mkdir` combined with the check of the options set in npmrc
   * configurable through `.npmrc`
   * set to false by default
   * allow to change the attribute name and value to use this for other backup solution on unix (e.g. rsync), windows which support extended attributes
   * 
3. add a new hook which can be used in `.pnpmfile.cjs`
   * trigger any kind of task after a new `node_module` folder was created

* extended attributes are supported by all unix operating system and not MacOS specific
* only the name and value are MacOS specific but respected by nearly all backup solutions for MacOS
* Time Machine for MacOS and this attribute exists for more than a decade and will not change in the near future as the best main backup solution under MacOS
* Windows NTFS Supports extended attributes and uses the `Offline` attribute to exclude from Windows Backup and Restore

**Risks are:**
* filesystem does not support or application has not enough access rights - a warning for the developer should be ok in there cases

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

[asimov](https://github.com/stevegrunwell/asimov) - scanning your filesystem for known dependency directories (node_modules, vendors,..) and excludes them from backup, can run as cron job
[tmignore](https://github.com/samuelmeuli/tmignore) - excludes files and directories matched by .gitignore files, can run as cron job
